speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To evaluate this newborn with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting, which has passed meconium within the first 48 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of pyloric stenosis, could you confirm if this vomiting is truly bilious (green) and if the newborn has passed meconium? Also, has abdominal distension or palpable masses been noted on examination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. Has the baby passed any stool since the initial meconium, and is there visible abdominal distension during the physical exam?
